notes: SDSS J090745.0+024507 — The paper explicitly calls this object an unbound hyper-velocity star and states that its radial velocity alone substantially exceeds the Galactic escape velocity (T:p1-b0, T:p1-b3, T:p1-b7); the unbound candidacy is retained in the paper's assessment. The same target is abbreviated 'the HVS'; T:p2-b4 prints its SDSS designation as 'SDSS 090745.0+024507' (without the J), treated as a variant of the canonical identifier. No Gaia source identifier is supplied; GAIA is mentioned only as a future proper-motion mission. No other individually identifiable star is reported as a Galactic unbound candidate.

SDSS J090745.0+024507: No parallax or bound/unbound probabilities are reported. The paper gives only total proper motions, not separate RA/Dec components: predicted ∼0.3 (d/55) mas/yr, USNOB1 14±12 mas/yr, GSC2.3.1 20±11 mas/yr, and average 3±8 mas/yr (T:p4-b1), so proper-motion components are not recorded. The +709 km/s value (T:p1-b3, T:p2-b4) is the line-of-sight velocity in the Galactic rest frame, not the total three-dimensional speed, and the U,V,W components in T:p2-b7 are not a total speed; therefore no galactic_rest_frame_velocity value is recorded. The 39 kpc BHB distance is treated by the authors as a lower limit (T:p3-b3).
